actions.shape.ungroup: Name of the Ungroup action in the command palette and shortcut settings. Ungroup turns a placed shape (a box of marchers) back into plain marchers: they stay where they are and stop moving as one shape from that page on.
actions.shape.ungroupKeywords: Search words for the Ungroup action in the command palette, separated by spaces. Not shown; translate as words people might type to find it.
audio.contextMenu.beat.errorCreatingMeas: Error toast when "Mark as Measure" in a beat's right-click menu on the timeline fails to start a new measure at that beat.
fieldDisplay.caption.direction: Very short caption under the Field direction button in the field display bar (one word if possible): which way the field faces on screen.
fieldDisplay.caption.sections: Very short caption under the Visible sections button in the field display bar (one word if possible). Sections are groups of the band, such as trumpets or color guard.
fieldDisplay.comingSoon: Shown in the tooltip and screen-reader label of field display bar buttons that are not available yet.
fieldDisplay.direction: Tooltip name of a field display bar button that will turn which way the field faces on screen (for example, the audience at the bottom or the top). The button is not available yet.
fieldDisplay.label: Screen-reader label for the field display bar, a column of small buttons at the top right of the field that change what the field shows (marcher labels, shape outlines and so on).
fieldDisplay.sections: Tooltip name of a field display bar button that will choose which sections of the band are shown on the field. The button is not available yet.
launchpage.learn.troubleshooting.refresh: Troubleshooting tip on the Learn page of the start screen: reloading the app often fixes problems. <keys></keys> is replaced by the reload keyboard shortcut, shown as a key (Command-R on a Mac, Ctrl+R elsewhere).
library.import.choices.grip.picking: Label of the grip button while the import waits for the person to click a point on the 3D model (the grip is where a performer holds the prop). Pressing the button again or the key stops picking. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key, shown as a key.
library.import.stage.pickGrip: Hint over the 3D preview while importing a prop model, after the person chose to set the grip (where a performer holds the prop): they click the point on the model. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key, shown as a key.
marchers.csv.info: Help text at the top of the form that imports marchers from a CSV (spreadsheet) file. Says which columns can be left empty, that rows with errors aren't imported, and that the import can be undone. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Undo keyboard shortcut, shown as a key (Command-Z on a Mac, Ctrl+Z elsewhere).
marchers.deleteWarning: Confirmation message before deleting marchers from the marcher list. {marchers} is a comma-separated list of the marchers' drill numbers (such as T1, T2). <keys></keys> is replaced by the Undo keyboard shortcut, shown as a key (Command-Z on a Mac, Ctrl+Z elsewhere).
music.undoWithCtrlZ: Note under a tempo change on its card in the music editor, telling the person the change can be reversed. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Undo keyboard shortcut, shown as a key (Command-Z on a Mac, Ctrl+Z elsewhere).
settings.shortcuts.conflict: Warning in the keyboard shortcuts settings when the shortcut just pressed already belongs to other actions. <keys></keys> is replaced by that shortcut, shown as a key; {actions} is a comma-separated list of the action names that use it. {binding} is the same shortcut as plain text, kept for older translations.
settings.shortcuts.recording: Status shown in a row of the keyboard shortcuts settings while the app waits for the person to press the new shortcut. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key, shown as a key.
shapes.edit.drawHint: Hint shown over the field after picking a shape kind on the Shapes tab, before drawing it. {shape} is the shape's name in lowercase (for example box or circle). <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key, shown as a key.
shapes.edit.ungroup: Tooltip of the Ungroup button in the floating bar shown over a selected shape on the field. Clicking it turns the shape back into plain marchers who keep their spots.
shapes.placed.ungroupError: Error toast when ungrouping a placed shape (turning it back into plain marchers) fails.
shapes.placed.ungroupIsolated: Error toast when Ungroup is used while one move on the timeline is isolated, on a shape that was made on an earlier page. The user has to leave isolation first.
shapes.tool.tab.ringHint: Hint beside the shape buttons on the Shapes toolbar tab. <keys></keys> is replaced by the keyboard shortcut (shown as a key) that opens the shape ring, a round menu of shapes; the person holds that key with the pointer over the field. {key} is the same shortcut as plain text, kept for older translations.
shortcut.gesture.click: The word for a mouse or trackpad gesture inside a keyboard shortcut, written after the keys, as in “Shift + click” (hold Shift while you click). Lowercase unless your language capitalizes it here. Keep it short: it sits inside a small key-shaped label.
shortcut.gesture.drag: The word for a mouse or trackpad gesture inside a keyboard shortcut, written after the keys, as in “Shift + drag” (hold Shift while you drag). Lowercase unless your language capitalizes it here. Keep it short: it sits inside a small key-shaped label.
shortcut.gesture.scroll: The word for a mouse or trackpad gesture inside a keyboard shortcut, written after the keys, as in “Shift + scroll” (hold Shift while you scroll). Lowercase unless your language capitalizes it here. Keep it short: it sits inside a small key-shaped label.
tempoMode.band.action.aTempo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that returns to the tempo from before a gradual change ("a tempo" is the Italian music term, keep it as musicians in your language write it). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.addedChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that adds a tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo starts). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.countsHalfAsFast: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that makes the selected counts (beats) half as fast. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.countsTwiceAsFast: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that makes the selected counts (beats) twice as fast. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.curve: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that bends a gradual tempo change (ramp) into a curve. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.endsOn: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit made by dragging the end of a stretch of the tempo line up or down: the stretch ends on {tempo}, which is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120". Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.endsOnThen: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit made by dragging the end of a stretch of the tempo line up or down: the stretch ends on {tempo}, then the music jumps to {next}. Both is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120". Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.gradual: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that turns a jump in tempo into a gradual change (a ramp, like a ritardando or accelerando). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.held: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that sets how long a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time) lasts. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {seconds} is a number of seconds; "s" is the unit. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.hold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that makes a count a hold or not. A hold (fermata) is a count held for a length of time in seconds instead of played at a tempo. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.holdDrill: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that ends a move one count early so the marchers stand still for a count (a breath), without changing the music. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.jump: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that turns a gradual tempo change (ramp) back into a sudden jump to the new tempo. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.measureNumber: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that renumbers measures by hand. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.movedChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit made by dragging a tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo starts) sideways to another count. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.musicStart: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that moves where the music starts against count 1. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.pin: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that pins or unpins a count. A pin locks a count to a spot in the music, so tempo edits around it never move it. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.pinned: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit made by dragging a count onto its spot in the music, which pins it there (locks it to that spot). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.pins: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that removes all pins at once. A pin locks a count to a spot in the music. Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.rehearsalMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of an edit to a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section, such as "C"). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.removedChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that removes a tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo starts); the tempo before it carries on. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.tempo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of an edit to the tempo (speed of the counts). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.action.timeSignature: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), name of the edit that sets a time signature (such as 4/4 or 7/8). Its text is also used as {action} in the error toast "{action}: {error}" when the edit fails.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.intro: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), explanation at the top of the box for adding counts (beats). The audio recording is never edited.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.keepMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when adding a count: the measure gets one more count in the same time, so its counts get faster. {measure} is a measure such as "m. 12". {count} is its new number of counts. {tempo} is the tempo before and after, such as "♩120 → ♩150".
tempoMode.band.ask.add.keepWhole: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when adding counts: the counts between two pins (counts locked to the music) squeeze to fit the new ones, so they take the same time and get faster. {range} is the span of counts, such as "m. 11 count 1 to m. 12 count 4". {tempo} is the tempo before and after, such as "♩120 → ♩135".
tempoMode.band.ask.add.manyKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts where several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each keeps its length and its marchers stand still for the added counts at its end. {moves} is the number of moves (always 2 or more); {count} is how many counts are added.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.manyShift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts where several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each gets longer. {moves} is the number of moves (always 2 or more); {count} is how many counts are added.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.needPin: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), why an option to add counts is unavailable: there must be a pinned count (one locked to a spot in the music) after the spot, to fix the length of music the counts must fit into.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.noMove: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts where no move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) is: the marchers simply stand still during the added counts.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.oneKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) over the spot keeps its length, and its marchers stand still for the added counts at its end. {move} names the move, such as "Its move", "Page 11's move" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {moveCounts} is the move's length in counts; {count} is how many counts are added.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.oneShift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when adding counts: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) over the spot gets longer. {move} names the move, such as "Its move", "Page 11's move" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {from} and {to} are its length in counts before and after.
tempoMode.band.ask.add.shift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when adding counts: the new counts add time, so everything after moves later against the music. Use it when the counts after were ahead of the music. {seconds} is the time added in seconds; "s" is the unit.
tempoMode.band.ask.addCountAfter: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a box offering ways to add a count (beat), for when the music has a beat the counts miss. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.ask.addCountBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a box offering ways to add a count (beat), for when the music has a beat the counts miss. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.ask.addMeasureBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a box offering ways to add a measure. Shown when the music has a beat the counts miss. {count} is how many counts (beats) the measure has. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.ask.addedCountAfter: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after adding a count (beat). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.ask.addedCountBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after adding a count (beat). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.ask.addedMeasureBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after adding a measure. {count} is how many counts (beats) it has. {measure} is a measure number. Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.ask.breath.many: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), what the "hold the drill" option does when several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each ends a count early and the marchers stand still for that count. Also shown alone as a toast once done. {moves} is the number of moves (2 or more).
tempoMode.band.ask.breath.noCountAdded: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of the "hold the drill" option when adding a count: instead of adding a count, the move ends a count early so marchers stand still (a breath).
tempoMode.band.ask.breath.none: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), why the "hold the drill" option is unavailable: no move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) runs over this spot, so there is nothing to end early.
tempoMode.band.ask.breath.one: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), what the "hold the drill" option does: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) gets one count shorter and the marchers stand still on its last count. Also shown alone as a toast once done. {move} names the move, such as "Page 11" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {from} and {to} are its length in counts before and after. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). It may end with ", before C" naming the next rehearsal mark.
tempoMode.band.ask.countsFewer: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), when counts are removed where no page is: how many fewer counts (beats) the show has. Shown as a sentence on its own.
tempoMode.band.ask.countsMore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), when counts are added where no page is: how many more counts (beats) the show gets. Shown as a sentence on its own.
tempoMode.band.ask.laterCountsStay: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence in an option when adding or removing counts: the counts after the change stay where they are against the music. Use it when they already line up with the music.
tempoMode.band.ask.noMoveHere: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), very short reason the "hold the drill" option is unavailable: there is no move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) here.
tempoMode.band.ask.noPinAfter: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), very short reason an option is unavailable when adding or removing counts: there is no pinned count (one locked to a spot in the music) after the spot.
tempoMode.band.ask.pageCounts: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), how a page's length in counts (beats) changes when counts are added or removed. {page} is the page's name, such as "11"; {from} is its count now and {to} after. Several may be listed, separated by ", ".
tempoMode.band.ask.pagesSentence: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), turns a list of page changes into a sentence in the explanation of adding or removing counts. {pages} is one or more items like "Page 11: 8 → 9 counts" separated by ", ", or a phrase like "1 count more". Only change the full stop if your language ends sentences differently.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.intro: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), explanation at the top of the box for removing counts (beats). The audio recording is never edited.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.keep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when removing counts: the remaining counts nearby stretch to fill the same time, so they get slower. {where} is the measure or span, such as "m. 12" or "m. 11 count 1 to m. 12 count 4". {from} and {to} are the number of counts before and after. {tempo} is the tempo before and after, such as "♩120 → ♩90".
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.manyKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts where several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each keeps its length by ending later. {moves} is the number of moves (2 or more).
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.manyShift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts where several moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) overlap: each gets shorter. {moves} is the number of moves (2 or more).
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.needPin: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), why an option to remove counts is unavailable: there must be a pinned count (one locked to a spot in the music) after the spot, to fix the length of music the counts must fill.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.noMove: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts where no move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) is.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.oneKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) over them keeps its length by ending later. {move} names the move, such as "Its move", "Page 11's move" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {moveCounts} is its length in counts; {count} is how many counts are removed.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.oneShift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence when removing counts: the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) over them gets shorter. {move} names the move, such as "Its move", "Page 11's move" or "The move from m. 3 count 1". {count} is how many counts are removed.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.shift: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), first sentence of an option when removing counts: their time is removed too, so everything after moves earlier against the music. Use it when the counts after were behind the music.
tempoMode.band.ask.remove.title: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a box offering ways to remove counts (beats), for when the music has fewer beats than counts. {where} is a count or span of counts such as "m. 12 count 3" or "m. 11 count 1 to m. 11 count 4".
tempoMode.band.ask.removed: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after removing counts (beats). {where} is a count or span of counts such as "m. 12 count 3" or "m. 11 count 1 to m. 11 count 4". Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.drag.cantPut: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), red label while dragging a spot in the music onto a count where it can't go. {count} is the count (beat) number from the start of the show. {reason} is why, already translated, such as "count 5 is pinned: the counts between would pass 400 BPM".
tempoMode.band.drag.hitToCountOne: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label shown while dragging a hit (a clear beat or accent in the music) onto count 1, the start of the show: dropping it moves where the music starts.
tempoMode.band.drag.spotToCountOne: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label shown while dragging the line of count 1 (the start of the show) along the music: dropping it moves where the music starts.
tempoMode.band.drag.stops: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), red label while dragging a count line that has reached as far as it can go. {reason} is why, already translated, such as "count 5 is pinned".
tempoMode.band.editor.holdHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a text box for the length of a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time instead of played at a tempo). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.editor.markHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a text box for naming a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section, such as "C"). Leaving the box empty removes the mark. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.editor.notATempo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing a tempo that can't be read. {value} is what was typed. "120-90" means a gradual change from 120 to 90 beats a minute; keep the numbers and the hyphen.
tempoMode.band.editor.renumberHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a text box for giving a measure a number by hand; the measures after it are numbered on from there. Leaving it empty goes back to automatic numbering. "m." is short for measure. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.editor.tempoFromToHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a small text box for typing the tempo (beats a minute) of a span of counts. "120-90" means a gradual change from 120 to 90; keep the examples as they are. {from} and {to} are places like "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.editor.tempoOfHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above a small text box for typing the tempo (beats a minute) of one count. "120-90" means a gradual change from 120 to 90; keep the examples as they are. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.editor.tempoOutOfRange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing a tempo outside the allowed range. {value} is what was typed.
tempoMode.band.editor.wholeStretch: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), link under the tempo text box: edit the tempo of the whole stretch (all the counts at this tempo) instead of just these counts. {range} is a span such as "m. 11 count 1 to m. 14 count 4". {tempo} is its tempo now, a number like "120" or "120-90" for a gradual change; ♩ is a quarter-note symbol.
tempoMode.band.label.aHold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), what a stretch of counts is when it is only a hold (a fermata: a count held for a length of time instead of played at a tempo). Shown in place of a tempo, as {now} or {was} in "now {now} (was {was})".
tempoMode.band.label.beforeMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), where marchers hold, when a rehearsal mark starts right after it. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {mark} is a rehearsal mark: a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section, such as "C".
tempoMode.band.label.count: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a place in the show before any measure starts, used inside other messages. {count} is the count (beat) number from the start of the show. A count is one beat of the drill.
tempoMode.band.label.measure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a measure, short form, used inside other messages and as a title. "m." is short for measure. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.label.measureCount: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a place in the show, used inside many other messages. "m." is short for measure. {measure} is a measure number. {count} is the count (beat) within that measure, from 1.
tempoMode.band.label.measures: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a span of measures, short form, such as "m. 11–12". Used as a title and in the Play button's tooltip. {from} and {to} are the first and last measure numbers.
tempoMode.band.label.range: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), a span of counts, used inside other messages. {from} and {to} are places like "m. 11 count 1" (first and last count of the span).
tempoMode.band.label.respacedShort: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), the short form of "{range}: now {now} (was {was})" when there is no room: the tempo of re-spaced counts now and before. {now} and {was} are tempos such as "♩120" or "♩70→60", or the words "a hold".
tempoMode.band.label.respacedStretch: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), after dragging a count onto the music, names counts whose spacing changed and their tempo now and before. Shown on the tempo lane during the drag and listed in a toast. {range} is a span of counts such as "m. 11 count 1 to m. 12 count 4". {now} and {was} are tempos such as "♩120", "♩70→60" (a gradual change) or "♩68–74" (uneven), or the words "a hold".
tempoMode.band.lane.clearSelection: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), screen-reader label of a small round × button at the end of the selected counts, which deselects them.
tempoMode.band.lane.clearSelectionTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip of a small round × button at the end of the selected counts, which deselects them. {key} is the keyboard key that does the same, such as "Esc".
tempoMode.band.lane.holdLabel: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), small label on the tempo lane over a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time): how long it is held. {seconds} is a number; "s" is the unit (seconds). Keep it short.
tempoMode.band.lane.holdLabelShort: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), the shortest label over a hold (fermata) on the tempo lane, when there is no room for "hold". {seconds} is a number; "s" is the unit (seconds).
tempoMode.band.lane.markDrag: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label shown while dragging a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) to another measure: where it would land. {mark} is the mark, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is the measure number, or "?".
tempoMode.band.lane.markTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section) in the marks lane. {mark} is the mark, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.lane.renumberedTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a measure number that was set by hand. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.lane.shortMeasureTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a measure number marked with an asterisk: the measure has fewer counts than its time signature. {measure} is a measure number. {count} is its number of counts (beats).
tempoMode.band.lane.timeSignatureTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip on a time signature chip in the measures lane. {meter} is the time signature, such as "4/4" or "7/8 (2+2+3)".
tempoMode.band.menu.aTempo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item: go back to the tempo from before a gradual change. "A tempo" is the Italian music term; keep it as musicians in your language write it.
tempoMode.band.menu.aTempoAside: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text at the right of the "A tempo" menu item: the tempo it goes back to. {tempo} is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120".
tempoMode.band.menu.aTempoHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), hint on the "A tempo" menu item (go back to the tempo from before a gradual change). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.menu.addChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that adds a tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo can start) at this count, without changing any tempo yet.
tempoMode.band.menu.addCountAfter: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to add a count (beat) after this one, for when the music has a beat the counts miss.
tempoMode.band.menu.addCountBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to add a count (beat) before this one, for when the music has a beat the counts miss.
tempoMode.band.menu.addMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to put a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section) on this measure.
tempoMode.band.menu.addMeasureBefore: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to add a measure before this one, for when the music has beats the counts miss.
tempoMode.band.menu.cancel: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item that closes the menu without doing anything.
tempoMode.band.menu.clearSelection: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that deselects the selected counts.
tempoMode.band.menu.countTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the right-click menu for one count (beat). "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number. {count} is the count within that measure, from 1.
tempoMode.band.menu.countTitleNoMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the right-click menu for a count (beat) before any measure. {count} is its number from the start of the show.
tempoMode.band.menu.editMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to rename or remove this measure's rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section).
tempoMode.band.menu.gradual: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item (unavailable here) that would make the tempo change gradually (a ramp, like a ritardando or accelerando) to the tempo after it.
tempoMode.band.menu.gradualHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), hint on the "Gradual change to …" menu item. Holds (fermatas) and pins (counts locked to the music) outside the stretch don't change. {tempo} is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120".
tempoMode.band.menu.gradualNothingHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), hint on the unavailable "Gradual change" menu item: why there is no gradual change to make.
tempoMode.band.menu.gradualTo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that makes the tempo change gradually (a ramp, like a ritardando or accelerando) to the tempo after this stretch. {tempo} is a tempo written as a quarter-note symbol and a number, such as "♩120".
tempoMode.band.menu.halfAsFast: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that makes the selected counts (beats) half as fast.
tempoMode.band.menu.holdLength: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to type how long a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time) lasts.
tempoMode.band.menu.holdSubtitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside the menu title of a count that is a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time): how long it is held. {seconds} is a number; "s" is the unit (seconds).
tempoMode.band.menu.makeHold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that makes the count a hold: held for a length of time in seconds instead of played at a tempo (a fermata in music).
tempoMode.band.menu.markMoveHere: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item: move a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) from another measure to this one. {mark} is the name, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is the measure it is on now.
tempoMode.band.menu.markTaken: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of a small menu after naming a rehearsal mark (a letter or name printed in the score to mark a section) with a name another measure already has. {mark} is the name, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.menu.markUseAgain: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item: give this measure the same rehearsal mark (section letter or name) as another measure. {mark} is the name, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.menu.measureSubtitleMark: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside a measure's menu title: its time signature and rehearsal mark. {meter} is a time signature such as "4/4" or "7/8 (2+2+3)". {mark} is the rehearsal mark (section letter or name), such as "C".
tempoMode.band.menu.measureTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the right-click menu for a measure. {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.menu.notAHold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that turns a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time) back into an ordinary count.
tempoMode.band.menu.pin: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that pins the count: locks it to its spot in the music, so tempo edits around it never move it.
tempoMode.band.menu.removeChange: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that removes the tempo change (a point on the tempo line where a new tempo starts) at this count; the tempo before it carries on.
tempoMode.band.menu.removeCount: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to remove this count (beat), for when the music has fewer beats than counts.
tempoMode.band.menu.removeCounts: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to remove the selected counts (beats).
tempoMode.band.menu.removeMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to remove this measure's counts, for when the music has fewer beats than counts.
tempoMode.band.menu.renumber: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to number this measure by hand; the measures after are numbered on from it.
tempoMode.band.menu.seconds: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet value at the right of a menu item: a length in seconds. "s" is the unit.
tempoMode.band.menu.selectionCounts: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside the title of the right-click menu for selected counts: how many counts (beats) are selected.
tempoMode.band.menu.setTempo: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that opens a box to type the tempo (beats a minute) of the counts.
tempoMode.band.menu.timeSignature: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item on a measure that opens a menu of time signatures (such as 4/4 or 7/8).
tempoMode.band.menu.toMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text at the right of the "Set tempo…" menu item: the tempo would be set up to this measure. "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.menu.twiceAsFast: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that makes the selected counts (beats) twice as fast.
tempoMode.band.menu.unpin: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), right-click menu item that unpins the count: it is no longer locked to its spot in the music.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.counted: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item choosing a time signature with how its eighth notes are grouped into counts. {meter} is a time signature such as "7/8"; {grouping} is the grouping such as "2+2+3".
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.fromSubtitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside the time signature menu title: the choice lasts until the next time signature.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.fromTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the time signature menu: the choice applies from this measure. "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.justThisMeasure: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item that switches on or off (with a check mark) whether the chosen time signature applies to this measure only.
In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), hint on the "Just this measure" menu item.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.onlySubtitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), quiet text beside the time signature menu title when "Just this measure" is on: the measures after keep their time signatures.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.onlyTitle: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), title of the time signature menu when "Just this measure" is on. "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.other: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), menu item that opens a box to type any time signature with its grouping of eighth notes. Keep the example as it is.
tempoMode.band.meterMenu.otherHint: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), label above the text box for typing a time signature and how its eighth notes are grouped into counts. Keep the examples as they are.
tempoMode.band.move.from: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), names a move (a stretch of drill where marchers travel between positions) that starts on no page, by where it starts. Used as the subject of a sentence, as {move} in other messages. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.move.its: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), the subject of a sentence about the move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) of the page just named, as {move} in other messages. "Its" is the page.
tempoMode.band.move.page: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), names a move (a stretch of drill where marchers travel between positions) by the page it starts on. Used as the subject of a sentence, as {move} in other messages. {page} is the page's name, such as "11" or "11A".
tempoMode.band.move.pagesMove: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), the move (a stretch of drill where marchers travel) that starts on a page, as the subject of a sentence ({move} in other messages). {page} is the page's name, such as "11".
tempoMode.band.tip.outlier: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), tooltip over a red dot on the tempo line, marking a count much faster or slower than the counts either side. Its line may have been dragged onto the wrong hit (a clear beat or accent in the music). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {direction} chooses "faster" or "slower". {tempo}, {before} and {after} are tempos such as "♩120".
tempoMode.band.toast.addCountsFirst: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast when trying to name or renumber a measure past the end of the show, where no counts exist yet.
tempoMode.band.toast.failed: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast when an edit fails. {action} names the edit (such as "Tempo" or "Pinned m. 3 count 1 to the music"); {error} is the reason, already translated.
tempoMode.band.toast.holdInvalid: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing a hold length that isn't a number of seconds between 0.05 and 600. A hold is a fermata: a count held for a length of time.
tempoMode.band.toast.holdMade: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after making a count a hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time instead of played at a tempo). It explains how to set its length: drag the line of the next count, or its hit (a clear beat in the music), to where the music continues. {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.toast.markAlreadyThere: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after dragging a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) onto a measure that has one. "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number. {mark} is that measure's mark, such as "C".
tempoMode.band.toast.markDropped: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after pressing M while the music plays, which puts a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) on the nearest measure. {mark} is the mark's name, such as "C". {measure} is a measure number.
tempoMode.band.toast.markMoved: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after dragging a rehearsal mark (section letter or name) to another measure. {mark} is the mark, such as "C". "m." is short for measure; {from} and {to} are measure numbers.
tempoMode.band.toast.meterPinsNote: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence added to the toast after setting a time signature that changed count lengths: pins (counts locked to the music) inside were removed. {count} is how many.
tempoMode.band.toast.meterSetFrom: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after setting a time signature from a measure until the next time signature. {meter} is the time signature, such as "7/8 (2+2+3)". {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {count} is how many counts (beats) each measure now has. Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.toast.meterSetOnly: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after setting a time signature for one measure only. {meter} is the time signature, such as "2/4" or "7/8 (2+2+3)". "m." is short for measure; {measure} is a measure number. Further sentences may follow, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.toast.meterShiftNote: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence added to the toast after setting a time signature for one measure: the measures after it move. {count} is by how many counts (beats); {direction} chooses "earlier" or "later".
tempoMode.band.toast.meterShortNote: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), sentence added to the toast after setting a time signature: the counts didn't divide evenly, so the last measure has fewer counts; it is marked with an asterisk (*) in the measures lane. {count} is its number of counts.
tempoMode.band.toast.movesCouldNotKeep: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), part of the toast after adding or removing counts: how many moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) had to get longer or shorter. Shown after the edit's name, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.toast.movesKept: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), part of the toast after adding or removing counts: how many moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) kept their number of counts. Shown after the edit's name, separated by ". ".
tempoMode.band.toast.movesKeptHold: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), part of the toast after adding counts that fit into the same stretch of music: the moves (stretches of drill where marchers travel) over the spot kept their length, so the marchers stand still for the added counts at the end. {kept} is the number of moves; {count} is the number of counts added.
tempoMode.band.toast.musicCantMove: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after dragging a spot in the music onto count 1 (which moves where the music starts). A pinned count is locked to a hit (a clear beat or accent in the music). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure).
tempoMode.band.toast.musicMoved: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after dragging a spot in the music onto count 1: the music now starts earlier or later against the counts. A hit is a clear beat or accent in the music. {seconds} is a number of seconds; "s" is the unit. {direction} chooses "earlier" or "later".
tempoMode.band.toast.musicMovedWithPins: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after dragging a spot in the music onto count 1 when some counts are pinned (locked to hits, clear beats in the music): they move with the music. {seconds} is a number of seconds; "s" is the unit. {direction} chooses "earlier" or "later".
tempoMode.band.toast.notATimeSignature: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing a time signature that can't be read. {text} is what was typed. "7/8 2+2+3" is a time signature followed by how its eighth notes are grouped into counts; keep the examples as they are.
tempoMode.band.toast.notMeasureNumber: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast after typing something that isn't a whole number when renumbering a measure. {value} is what was typed.
tempoMode.band.toast.pinsInSelection: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast when making the selected counts twice or half as fast while some of them are pinned (locked to a spot in the music).
tempoMode.band.toast.respaced: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after dragging a count onto the music re-spaced counts far from it. The count is pinned (locked to that spot). {where} is a place in the show written as a measure and count, such as "m. 12 count 3" ("m." is short for measure). {stretches} lists the re-spaced spans and their tempo, such as "m. 3 count 1 to m. 6 count 4: now ♩118 (was ♩120)", separated by "; ".
tempoMode.band.toast.tooFastOrSlow: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error toast when a tempo edit can't be made because a count would go faster than 400 or slower than 20 beats a minute. {action} names the edit (such as "Tempo" or "Ends on ♩120").
tempoMode.button.hint: Second line of the tempo mode button's tooltip while the mode is off: what the mode is for. Time signatures are e.g. 4/4 or 3/4; rehearsal marks are the letters (A, B, C…) printed in sheet music to name sections. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.button.hintOn: Second line of the tempo mode button's tooltip while the mode is on. <escape></escape> is replaced by a keycap showing the Escape key and <toggle></toggle> by a keycap showing Shift+T; either key leaves tempo mode. Keep the tags, each with nothing between them. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.button.label: Name of the button in the timeline's transport bar that turns tempo mode on and off; shown as its tooltip title and read by screen readers. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.button.labelOn: Tooltip title of the tempo mode button while tempo mode is on. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.button.text: Short visible text on the tempo mode button in the timeline's transport bar (next to a gauge icon). Keep it very short. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.errors.cantRemoveLastCount: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error shown in a toast when trying to remove the show's last count (beat).
tempoMode.errors.countPinned: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), reason a dragged count line stops or can't go somewhere: count {count} is pinned (locked to its spot in the music). Shown after "Stops here: " or "Can't put it on count N: ". {count} is a count (beat) number.
tempoMode.errors.holdTooShort: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), reason a dragged count line stops: the hold (fermata: a count held for a length of time) before it is already as short as allowed. BPM is beats per minute. Shown after "Stops here: " or "Can't put it on count N: ".
tempoMode.errors.keptCountOnMusic: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), toast after a tempo edit: count {count} is pinned (locked to a spot in the music), so the edited counts' tempo was changed to keep it there. {count} is a count (beat) number from the start of the show.
tempoMode.errors.moveOneCountLong: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error shown in a toast after "Hold the drill: " when a move (stretch of drill where marchers travel) can't end a count early because it is only one count long.
tempoMode.errors.tooFastAfterPin: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), reason a dragged count line stops: count {count} before it is pinned (locked to the music), and the counts between would get faster than 400 beats per minute (BPM). Shown after "Stops here: " or "Can't put it on count N: ".
tempoMode.errors.tooFastFromStart: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), reason a dragged count line stops: the counts between it and the start of the show would get faster than 400 beats per minute (BPM). Shown after "Stops here: " or "Can't put it on count N: ".
tempoMode.errors.tooSlowAfterPin: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), reason a dragged count line stops: count {count} before it is pinned (locked to the music), and the counts between would get slower than 20 beats per minute (BPM). Shown after "Stops here: " or "Can't put it on count N: ".
tempoMode.errors.tooSlowFromStart: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), reason a dragged count line stops: the counts between it and the start of the show would get slower than 20 beats per minute (BPM). Shown after "Stops here: " or "Can't put it on count N: ".
tempoMode.errors.wouldRemovePage: In tempo mode (a timeline view for fitting the counts of a marching show to the music), error shown in a toast when removing counts would remove the start of a page (a section of the drill).
tempoMode.help.doubleClickLane.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Double-click the tempo lane or line". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. A tempo change is a point where the tempo changes, drawn as a dot on the tempo line. The tempo lane is the row showing the tempo line.
tempoMode.help.doubleClickLane.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "adds a tempo change there; double-click a change's dot to remove it" and completes it. A tempo change is a point where the tempo changes, drawn as a dot on the tempo line. The tempo lane is the row showing the tempo line.
tempoMode.help.dragChangeDot.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Drag a tempo change's dot". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. Dragging a tempo change's dot vertically sets its tempo; horizontally moves it to another count.
tempoMode.help.dragChangeDot.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "up or down for its tempo, sideways to move where it changes" and completes it. Dragging a tempo change's dot vertically sets its tempo; horizontally moves it to another count.
tempoMode.help.dragEndDot.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Drag a stretch's square end dot". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. A stretch is the span of counts between two tempo changes. 'rit.' (ritardando) is the musical term for gradually slowing down, and 'a tempo' is the musical term for returning to the original speed; use the usual musical terms in your language (often the Italian ones are kept). A pinned count is a count locked to a spot in the music, so it stays put while other counts are dragged.
tempoMode.help.dragEndDot.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "sets the tempo it ends on, so a rit. can jump back (a tempo); with a pinned count after it, the counts up to the pin make room" and completes it. A stretch is the span of counts between two tempo changes. 'rit.' (ritardando) is the musical term for gradually slowing down, and 'a tempo' is the musical term for returning to the original speed; use the usual musical terms in your language (often the Italian ones are kept). A pinned count is a count locked to a spot in the music, so it stays put while other counts are dragged.
tempoMode.help.dragHandle.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Drag a count's handle". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. Each count has a small triangle handle at the top of the music lane; dragging it moves that count to a point in the music.
tempoMode.help.dragHandle.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "(the triangle atop the music) onto the music" and completes it. Each count has a small triangle handle at the top of the music lane; dragging it moves that count to a point in the music.
tempoMode.help.dragLine.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Drag the tempo line". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. The tempo line is a graph of the tempo (beats per minute) over time. 'Set tempo…' is the name of an item in the right-click menu; translate it the same way as that menu item.
tempoMode.help.dragLine.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "up or down; right-click > Set tempo… to type one" and completes it. The tempo line is a graph of the tempo (beats per minute) over time. 'Set tempo…' is the name of an item in the right-click menu; translate it the same way as that menu item.
tempoMode.help.dragMark.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Drag a rehearsal mark". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. A rehearsal mark is a letter (A, B, C…) naming a section of the music; it can be dragged to another measure.
tempoMode.help.dragMark.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "to another measure" and completes it. A rehearsal mark is a letter (A, B, C…) naming a section of the music; it can be dragged to another measure.
tempoMode.help.dragMeasures.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Drag along Measures". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. 'Measures' is the name of a row (lane) in tempo mode showing measure numbers (bars of music); dragging along it selects counts.
tempoMode.help.dragMeasures.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "selects counts to edit" and completes it. 'Measures' is the name of a row (lane) in tempo mode showing measure numbers (bars of music); dragging along it selects counts.
tempoMode.help.dragMusic.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Drag a spot in the music". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. Drag a point in the music's waveform (e.g. a drum hit) sideways onto the count it should fall on; the tempo changes so that they line up.
tempoMode.help.dragMusic.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "onto its count" and completes it. Drag a point in the music's waveform (e.g. a drum hit) sideways onto the count it should fall on; the tempo changes so that they line up.
tempoMode.help.dragRoundHandle.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Drag a stretch's round handle". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. A stretch is the span of counts between two tempo changes. Each has a round handle; dragging it turns a sudden tempo jump into a gradual speeding up or slowing down. Double-clicking the handle turns it back into a sudden jump.
tempoMode.help.dragRoundHandle.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "makes a gradual change, straight or curved; double-click it for a jump again" and completes it. A stretch is the span of counts between two tempo changes. Each has a round handle; dragging it turns a sudden tempo jump into a gradual speeding up or slowing down. Double-clicking the handle turns it back into a sudden jump.
tempoMode.help.keys.escape: Help card, keyboard list: what the Escape key does in tempo mode, in order of priority: clear selected counts, else cancel a drag in progress, else close tempo mode.
tempoMode.help.keys.mark: Help card, keyboard list: what the M key does. A rehearsal mark is a letter (A, B, C…) naming a section of the music; pressing M while the music plays places the next one at the current measure.
tempoMode.help.keys.play: Help card, keyboard list: what the Space key does in tempo mode. The playhead is the vertical line marking the current time on the timeline.
tempoMode.help.keys.tap: Help card, keyboard list: what the T key does. Tap tempo is a tool where you tap a key in time with the music and it shows the speed in beats per minute.
tempoMode.help.keys.toggle: Help card, keyboard list: what Shift+T does: turns tempo mode on or off.
tempoMode.help.label: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the '?' button in tempo mode's header row. It opens a card explaining how tempo mode works. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.help.rightClick.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Right-click". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. Lists what the right-click menu offers. A pinned count is a count locked to a spot in the music, so it stays put while other counts are dragged. A hold (fermata) is a pause where the music or drill holds still for extra time.
tempoMode.help.rightClick.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "pins, holds, tempo changes, adding and removing counts" and completes it. Lists what the right-click menu offers. A pinned count is a count locked to a spot in the music, so it stays put while other counts are dragged. A hold (fermata) is a pause where the music or drill holds still for extra time.
tempoMode.help.rightClickGradual.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Right-click in a gradual change". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. A gradual change is a stretch where the tempo speeds up or slows down smoothly. 'A tempo' is the name of a right-click menu item and the musical term for returning to the original speed; translate it the same way as that menu item.
tempoMode.help.rightClickGradual.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "A tempo: back to the tempo it started at" and completes it. A gradual change is a stretch where the tempo speeds up or slows down smoothly. 'A tempo' is the name of a right-click menu item and the musical term for returning to the original speed; translate it the same way as that menu item.
tempoMode.help.rightClickMeasure.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Right-click a measure". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. Lists what the right-click menu of a measure (a bar of music) offers: renumbering the measures from that one, adding a rehearsal mark (a section letter), changing the time signature (e.g. 4/4).
tempoMode.help.rightClickMeasure.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "renumber from there (or double-click its number), rehearsal mark, time signature" and completes it. Lists what the right-click menu of a measure (a bar of music) offers: renumbering the measures from that one, adding a rehearsal mark (a section letter), changing the time signature (e.g. 4/4).
tempoMode.help.shiftDrag.effect: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the right column, describing the result of the gesture shown at its left, "Shift while dragging". It may read as a continuation of that phrase or stand on its own. Holding Shift while dragging a count moves only that one count instead of stretching the counts around it.
tempoMode.help.shiftDrag.gesture: Help card in tempo mode, a two-column list of gestures: this is the left, bold column naming a gesture. The right column, shown beside it, reads "moves just that count" and completes it. Holding Shift while dragging a count moves only that one count instead of stretching the counts around it.
tempoMode.help.title: Heading of the help card that opens from the '?' button in tempo mode's header: the mode's purpose, getting the drill's counts to line up with the beats of the recorded music. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count). Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.lanes.marks.name: Name of a row (lane) in tempo mode, in a very narrow column (about 40 px) at the left of the timeline; abbreviate as needed. This lane shows rehearsal marks (letters A, B, C… naming sections of the music). Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.lanes.marks.title: Tooltip on the name of a row (lane) in tempo mode, explaining what the lane shows and what you can do in it. This lane shows rehearsal marks (letters A, B, C… naming sections of the music). Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.lanes.measures.name: Name of a row (lane) in tempo mode, in a very narrow column (about 40 px) at the left of the timeline; abbreviate as needed. This lane shows measures (bars of music) and their numbers and time signatures. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.lanes.measures.title: Tooltip on the name of a row (lane) in tempo mode, explaining what the lane shows and what you can do in it. This lane shows measures (bars of music) and their numbers and time signatures. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording. A time signature is e.g. 4/4 or 3/4.
tempoMode.lanes.music.name: Name of a row (lane) in tempo mode, in a very narrow column (about 40 px) at the left of the timeline; abbreviate as needed. This lane shows the music's waveform. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.lanes.music.title: Tooltip on the name of a row (lane) in tempo mode, explaining what the lane shows and what you can do in it. This lane shows the music's waveform. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording. A hit is a clear sound in the music such as a drum hit. Each count has a small triangle handle at the top of this lane.
tempoMode.lanes.tempo.name: Name of a row (lane) in tempo mode, in a very narrow column (about 40 px) at the left of the timeline; abbreviate as needed. This lane shows the tempo line, a graph of the speed in beats per minute. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.lanes.tempo.title: Tooltip on the name of a row (lane) in tempo mode, explaining what the lane shows and what you can do in it. This lane shows the tempo line, a graph of the speed in beats per minute. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording. A tempo change is a point where the speed changes (a dot); a round handle on a stretch between changes makes the change gradual. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count).
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.footer: Small print at the bottom of the box that opens when adding or removing counts in tempo mode, explaining its choice cards. <enter></enter> is replaced by a keycap showing the Enter key and <escape></escape> by one showing the Escape key; keep the tags, each with nothing between them. 'The one marked' is the card showing the Enter keycap, which is the choice made last time. 'Undo' is the app's Undo command.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.hold: Title of a choice card in the box that opens when adding a count in tempo mode: instead of adding a count, make the drill (the marchers' movement) pause in place here. Clicking the card does it.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.holdIntro: Question shown above the last choice card in the box that opens when adding a count in tempo mode: the music has no extra beat here, but maybe the marchers need extra time (a pause) before the next part of the drill.
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.keep: Title of a choice card in a box that opens when adding or removing counts in tempo mode: the counts after the change stay where they are against the music. Clicking the card does it. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count).
tempoMode.popovers.countAsk.shift: Title of a choice card in a box that opens when adding or removing counts in tempo mode: everything after the change moves later or earlier by the time added or removed. Clicking the card does it.
