tempoMode.popovers.measureGlyph: A tiny icon in tempo mode's right-click menu showing a measure number, e.g. 'm34' for measure 34. {number} is the measure number. Use your language's usual one- or two-letter abbreviation for 'measure' (bar), with no space.
tempoMode.tap.average: Shown in the Tap tempo panel under the measured tempo. {bpm} is the average tempo in beats per minute with one decimal, e.g. 120.4. If you stop tapping for 2 seconds, the next tap starts a new measurement. 's' is the abbreviation for seconds.
tempoMode.tap.count: In the corner of the Tap tempo panel: how many taps have been made so far. {count} is that number.
tempoMode.tap.hint: Second line of the Tap tempo button's tooltip, explaining the tool: tap in time with the music to measure its approximate tempo (speed in beats per minute).
tempoMode.tap.instructions: Instruction in the Tap tempo panel before any taps. <key></key> is replaced by a keycap showing the T key; keep the tag, with nothing between. 'The button' is the large Tap button below it. Each beat = each beat of the music.
tempoMode.tap.name: Name of the Tap tempo tool in tempo mode's header row: on its button, as the button's tooltip and screen-reader label, and as the heading of its panel. Tap tempo: you tap a key or button in time with the music and it shows how fast the music is, in beats per minute.
tempoMode.tap.reset: Button in the Tap tempo panel that clears the taps so far and starts over.
tempoMode.tap.selectFirst: Tooltip on the disabled Use button of the Tap tempo panel when there are no counts to apply the tempo to: the user needs to select counts first. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count).
tempoMode.tap.setTarget: Tooltip on the Use button of the Tap tempo panel. {target} names the counts it will change, e.g. 'm. 3–12' (measures 3 to 12). ♩{bpm} is the tapped tempo: a quarter-note symbol followed by beats per minute, e.g. ♩120, or ♩– when nothing has been tapped. Keep '♩' as it is. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count).
tempoMode.tap.tap: The large button in the Tap tempo panel that you press in time with the music; also its screen-reader label. 'Tap' as a verb (press briefly).
tempoMode.tap.use: The Use button in the Tap tempo panel, before anything is tapped and with no counts to apply it to. Use = apply the tapped tempo.
tempoMode.tap.useBpm: The Use button in the Tap tempo panel, with no counts to apply it to. ♩{bpm} is the tapped tempo: a quarter-note symbol followed by beats per minute, e.g. ♩120. Keep '♩'. Use = apply the tapped tempo.
tempoMode.tap.useBpmOn: The Use button in the Tap tempo panel. ♩{bpm} is the tapped tempo: a quarter-note symbol and beats per minute, e.g. ♩120; keep '♩'. {target} names the counts it will change, e.g. 'm. 3–12' (measures 3 to 12). Text inside <muted></muted> is shown in lighter text; keep the tags around the matching part. Use = apply the tapped tempo to those counts.
tempoMode.tap.useHint: Second line of the Use button's tooltip in the Tap tempo panel: Use sets a steady, unchanging tempo on the selected counts, or if none are selected, on the stretch under the playhead (the vertical line marking the current time). A stretch is the span of counts between two tempo changes.
tempoMode.tap.useOn: The Use button in the Tap tempo panel before anything is tapped. Text inside <muted></muted> is shown in lighter text; keep the tags around the matching part. {target} names the counts it will change, e.g. 'm. 3–12' (measures 3 to 12). Use = apply the tapped tempo to those counts.
tempoMode.timeline.playFromPlayhead: Tooltip on the timeline's Play button while tempo mode is on and no measures are selected: plays the music from the playhead (the vertical line marking the current time) onward.
tempoMode.timeline.playLoop: Tooltip on the timeline's Play button while tempo mode is on and some measures are selected: plays those measures over and over. {measures} names them, e.g. 'm. 11–12' (measures 11 to 12). 'Loop' is a verb here.
tempoMode.timeline.stopHere: Tooltip on the timeline's Stop button while playing in tempo mode: stops playback and leaves the playhead (current time) where it stopped, instead of jumping back.
tempoMode.toolbar.done: Button at the right of tempo mode's header row (and its screen-reader label) that closes tempo mode and returns to the normal timeline.
tempoMode.toolbar.doneLabel: Tooltip title of the Done button at the right of tempo mode's header: closes tempo mode. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.toolbar.dragHint: Hint text in tempo mode's header row, the main thing to do in the mode: drag a hit in the music (a clear sound such as a drum hit, in the waveform) sideways onto the count it should fall on. A count is one beat of the drill.
tempoMode.toolbar.metronome: Button in tempo mode's header row (and its screen-reader label) that turns the metronome on and off: a click sound on every count, to hear whether the counts line up with the music.
tempoMode.toolbar.metronomeHint: Second line of the Metronome button's tooltip in tempo mode: what the metronome is for. A count is one beat of the drill (marchers take one step per count). 'Sit on the music' = line up with the beats of the music.
tempoMode.toolbar.metronomeOff: Tooltip title of the Metronome button in tempo mode's header while the metronome is off. The metronome plays a click on every count.
tempoMode.toolbar.metronomeOn: Tooltip title of the Metronome button in tempo mode's header while the metronome is on. The metronome plays a click on every count.
tempoMode.toolbar.title: Name of the mode, shown at the left of tempo mode's header row while the mode is open. Tempo mode is a mode of the timeline (the strip at the bottom of the window showing the show over time) for lining the show's counts up with its music recording.
tempoMode.toolbar.unpinAll: Button in tempo mode's header row, shown only when some counts are pinned: unpins all of them. Its count of pinned counts is shown beside it. A pinned count is a count locked to a spot in the music, so it stays put while other counts are dragged.
tempoMode.toolbar.unpinAllAria: Screen-reader label of the Unpin all button in tempo mode's header. {count} is the number of pinned counts. A pinned count is a count locked to a spot in the music, so it stays put while other counts are dragged.
tempoMode.toolbar.unpinAllHint: Second line of the Unpin all button's tooltip, explaining pins: pinned counts stay locked to their spot in the music when you drag other counts or use Tap tempo. A pinned count is a count locked to a spot in the music, so it stays put while other counts are dragged.
tempoMode.toolbar.unpinAllLabel: Tooltip title of the Unpin all button in tempo mode's header. {count} is the number of pinned counts (always at least 1). A pinned count is a count locked to a spot in the music, so it stays put while other counts are dragged.
timeline.fit.hint: Second line of the tooltip on the timeline's Fit the show button (which zooms the timeline to show the whole show). Says that pressing it again returns to the previous zoom, and how else to zoom: pinch on a trackpad, or scroll while holding a key. <keys></keys> is replaced by that key and the word for scrolling, shown as a key (Command + scroll on a Mac, Ctrl + scroll elsewhere).
timeline.focusNotice.body: Notice shown at the top of the window while the timeline has keyboard focus and the rest of the editor ignores input. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key, shown as a key.
timeline.focusNotice.exit: Button in the timeline focus notice that gives the keyboard back to the main editor (the field).
timeline.rangeMenu.setAsShown: Menu item in a page's right-click menu on the timeline. Stores the selected marchers' current on-field positions as set (fixed) positions on that page, so they stop following the move around them.
timeline.rangeMenu.setAsShownNone: Why "Set as shown" is unavailable, shown next to the disabled menu item. {page} is a page name such as "Page 3". "Set" means a marcher has a stored position on that page; "partway through a move" means the marcher is in the middle of a move there.
toolbar.collisions.collisionsToolbar: Screen-reader label for the Collisions toolbar section, which lists marchers who are too close together on the current page.
view3d.autoOpenPrompt.description: Second line of the 3D View's "open on launch" question card. Settings › General is the app settings section where the answer can be changed later.
view3d.autoOpenPrompt.no: Button answering no to the 3D View's "open on launch" question: the 3D View won't open by itself (it stays open for now).
view3d.autoOpenPrompt.title: Question in a card at the bottom right of the 3D View window, shown each time the window opens until answered: should the 3D View open by itself whenever a show is opened?
view3d.autoOpenPrompt.yes: Button answering yes to the 3D View's "open on launch" question: the 3D View will open by itself with every show.
visuals.cue.pickingPoint: Button label in the Visuals cue panel while the app waits for the person to click a point on the field, for a cue that needs a position. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Escape key, shown as a key.
web.welcome.backUpBody: Paragraph in the welcome dialog of the web version of OpenMarch, which keeps shows in the browser. Explains backing up. <keys></keys> is replaced by the Save keyboard shortcut, shown as a key (Command-S on a Mac, Ctrl+S elsewhere); {save} is the same shortcut as plain text, kept for older translations.
